account: RL-Math's weight change is tiny (0.24 % of weight norm) and acts through paired directions: adding the base's top-8 singular input-output pairs per matrix (about 12 % of the change's squared norm) at 1.5x reproduces RL (hard328 vote within 0.1 points of RL's; 0.88 of RL's per-sample gain on problems the cued base never solves; 48 vs 50.5 of 136 fresh 2026 problems), while random rank-8 edits of the same size do nothing, and each direction works only with its own input-output pair.

Those pairs read input directions that the base's own step-by-step text already drives (8-11x a random subspace), and they write directions that the base's next layer reads 1.67x above random, so they amplify a deliberation circuit the base already has rather than encode the reward: General-RL, which has no gradable answer, concentrates as much (top-8 share 0.127 vs 0.135), Think-SFT's change lies in the same input subspace (4.8x chance) and Code-RL's even more (5.2x Think-SFT's), and where the change concentrates follows Think-SFT, not IF-RL.

The first ~100 RL steps write an opening switch, to answer as a deliberation ('Okay', 'Wait') instead of answer-first; the three-token cue (or a one-tensor hand edit, 397 of 500) gives the base this switch at inference: 224 to 410.5 of 500 on MATH-500, within 1.4 points of step-100 RL, with step 100's cap-hit rate and vote gain; the switch acts per sample through the opening, so a deliberative opening is right at about the cued rate whatever produced it, and step 100 still gains 8.5 of 500 from the cue because the switch is not yet complete in its weights.

Steps 100-2,800 add a second, graded part spread over all layers (early layers add right answers, late layers make answers finish): every sample slips less per step, adding 42.5 of 500 on MATH-500 and 9-14 points on hard328, both both where the base already solves sometimes (81 % of the MATH-500 gap) and where it has 0 of 4 right; it is written per domain (Math's pairs give code only 0.2-0.5 of Code's own gain) and keeps the base's own right routes where RL loses them.

Inference cannot write this second part: T 1.0 instead of 0.6 only removes loops (0.52 of the plain base's T 0.6 answers past 4,096 tokens loop), and votes gain 0.07-0.11 per contested problem only because the base's wrong answers scatter (pair agreement 0.26), so the cued base's vote stays about 9 points below RL's on hard328 (195 vs 224 of 328, with no right sample on 26 of the 36 problems RL wins) and about 11 points below on MATH-500 at AI2's setting.

Claims that the change is an all-or-none per-sample switch, a termination-only dial, an outcome-reward signature, a code-format push or a copy of RL's outcomes fail because it is this shared opening switch plus a graded per-step reliability shift on the base's own routes.

consequences.claim: For each writer matrix (o, down), f = (rl.next - rand.next) / (basew.next - rand.next) places RL-Math 3.1's 8 written directions between random directions (0) and the base matrix's own top-8 directions (1), by how strongly the next layer's q, k, v, gate and up read them. Sentence 2 says RL amplifies a circuit the base already reads, but one far smaller than its dominant directions, so the median f is well above 0 and well below 1 (about a quarter of the way).
consequences.why_new: result-ad95af reports only RL's gain over random (1.67x mean); no fact or result places RL's written directions on the scale from random to the base's own top-8 directions
consequences.statistic: median over writer matrices of f = (rl.next - rand.next) / (basew.next - rand.next), unitless
consequences.rows: all test-half rows of xlisten (o and down writers, layers 0-30)
consequences.computation: 1) For each xlisten row compute f = (rl.next - rand.next) / (basew.next - rand.next). 2) Statistic = median of f over the rows. 3) 90 % interval: 2000 bootstrap resamples of the rows (matrices) with replacement, the median of f in each, 5th and 95th percentiles.
consequences.null: random written directions of the same matrices give f = 0 by construction; the base-spectrum alternative (RL writes along the base matrix's own top directions) gives f = 1

consequences.claim: Code-RL 3.1's final change lies in RL-Math 3.1's step-100 top-8 input subspace far more than in General-RL 3.0's step-100 top-8 input subspace. Sentences 2-3 say the input side of RL's pairs is the base's deliberation-text subspace, already found in the first 100 steps of a reasoning reward. General's step-100 change is a larger share of its final change (0.35 vs 0.12 of the final norm), so size alone would favor General.
consequences.why_new: F51 and F32 use the final Math 3.1 subspace and Think-SFT; no fact or result uses the step-100 subspaces, or compares a Math checkpoint with a General checkpoint
consequences.statistic: median over matrices of cap_right(code31>math31_s100) / cap_right(code31>general30_s100), unitless
consequences.rows: all test-half rows of cap (q, k, v, o, gate, up, down of all layers)
consequences.computation: 1) For each cap row, r = cap['code31>math31_s100']['cap_right'] / cap['code31>general30_s100']['cap_right']. 2) Statistic = median of r over rows. 3) 90 % interval: 2000 bootstrap resamples of matrices with replacement, the median in each, 5th and 95th percentiles.
consequences.null: any early RL subspace of rank 8 captures Code's change equally (ratio 1); size alone (General's step-100 change is 3x further along) predicts at most 1; base spectrum predicts about 1

consequences.claim: The per-matrix pattern of top-8 share (each module's median removed) is more alike across the reasoning-reward runs (Math 3.0, Math 3.1, Code 3.1) at step 100 than in the final models. Sentences 3-4 say the first 100 steps write one shared opening switch whatever the reasoning reward, while later steps write a graded part per run and domain. Smaller step-100 changes are noisier, so size alone predicts lower similarity at step 100, not higher.
consequences.why_new: F24 and F62 correlate only final models with IF and Think-SFT; no fact or result compares the step-100 and final similarity of the concentration pattern
consequences.statistic: mean over the 3 pairs (math30,math31), (math31,code31), (math30,code31) of [Spearman rho of the step-100 residual top-8 shares - Spearman rho of the final residual top-8 shares], unitless
consequences.computation: 1) For each key k in math30, math31, code31, math30_s100, math31_s100, code31_s100: residual = top8_share[k] minus the median of top8_share[k] over the rows of the same module (q,k,v,o,gate,up,down) in the matrix set used. 2) For each pair (a,b): d = Spearman(resid[a_s100], resid[b_s100]) - Spearman(resid[a], resid[b]). 3) Statistic = mean of the 3 d. 4) 90 % interval: 2000 bootstrap resamples of matrices with replacement, recomputing the module medians and the Spearman rhos in each, 5th and 95th percentiles.
consequences.null: step-100 and final patterns are equally alike (0); same difference for non-reasoning pairs (Math 3.1 with General 3.0: -0.06; with IF 3.0: -0.21); size/noise predicts below 0

weights_cell.statistic: median over matrices of cap_right(Delta_late, V_s100) = ||Delta_late V_s100||^2 / ||Delta_late||^2, unitless
weights_cell.models: base, RL-Math 3.1 step-100 checkpoint, RL-Math 3.1 final
weights_cell.matrices: all 224 (q, k, v, o, gate, up, down of 32 layers)
weights_cell.computation: For each matrix: D100 = W(step 100) - W(base); Delta_late = W(final) - W(step 100); V_s100 = top-8 right (input-side) singular vectors of D100 from its SVD; cap = ||Delta_late V_s100||_F^2 / ||Delta_late||_F^2. Report the median over the 224 matrices.
weights_cell.why: Sentences 2-4 say steps 100-2,800 write the graded part through the same base-driven inputs the first 100 steps found, so the late update lies in step 100's input subspace far above chance (8/4096 = 0.002), at least as much as another Math run's change does (math30>math31_s100 0.054). The alternative (late training writes new directions, or only the size of the change matters) predicts about the base-spectrum level of 0.01.
